title: Independence movements
examples: What caused the decolonisation of Africa?
Can you explain the process of India gaining independence?

explain.say: Today we will look at independence movements around the world. We will study how nations gained self-rule. Our first topic is India in 1947.
The British rule in India ended in 1947. This was a major moment in world history. India became a sovereign nation that could govern itself.
Next we look at African independence movements. Many African nations fought for freedom. They worked to end European control over their lands.
Decolonisation is the process of gaining self-rule. This happened across many parts of the world. It meant ending foreign control over a land.
A real-life example is Ghana's independence. It gained freedom from Britain in 1957. This inspired many other African nations.
A common mistake is thinking independence happened all at once. It was a long, complex process. Resistance and negotiation were both involved.

items: It involved many years of struggle

faq.a: It means a country taking back its own control from a ruling foreign power. It is the process of ending colonialism.
asks: What is the meaning of decolonisation?

faq.q: Was the Indian independence movement peaceful?
faq.a: No, it involved both peaceful protests and periods of more intense conflict. Many methods were used to achieve freedom.
asks: Did India fight for its freedom?
What methods were used in the Indian struggle?

faq.q: Did all African countries gain independence at the same time?
faq.a: No, the timing was very different for each nation. Some gained freedom decades apart.
asks: Was Africa independent all at once?
When did African nations become free?

faq.q: What was the main goal of these movements?
faq.a: The main goal was to establish self-governance, meaning the people in charge made their own laws and decisions.
asks: What did they want after independence?

faq.a: Colonialism is when one powerful country controls and governs another territory. It takes resources and power from the controlled area.
asks: What is the opposite of colonialism?
What does it mean to be colonized?

facts: India gained independence from Britain in 1947.
Decolonisation was a global process affecting many parts of Africa and Asia.
Self-rule meant a nation could govern its own affairs.
The struggle for independence used many forms of protest.

quiz.say: The process of a colony gaining self-rule is called:
quiz.why: This term specifically describes the end of foreign control.

wrong.0: A revolution is a sudden, violent change, but decolonisation was often slower.
wrong.2: This word describes the act of controlling another place.
wrong.3: This is the state of being independent, not the process.

quiz.say: India achieved independence from which country in 1947?
quiz.why: Historical records confirm that Britain was the ruling power that left in 1947.

wrong.0: The US was not the primary colonial power in India.
wrong.1: China's history is separate from the British rule in India.
wrong.3: France had different colonial holdings, not India in this context.

quiz.say: If a country is moving towards self-rule, it is undergoing:
quiz.why: This is the correct term for the transition away from foreign control.

wrong.0: Annexation is the act of taking territory, not the process of gaining freedom.
wrong.1: Settlement describes where people live, not the political status of the land.
wrong.3: Imperialism is the policy of controlling others, the opposite action.
